intro: Civil engineers solve complex design problems, analyze systems and manage tight schedules, skills used across engineering and construction. The closest of the 25 careers below is Architects, Except Landscape and Naval, with an 81% skill match, while Construction Managers are 80% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $114,990, or 14% more.
why_it_works: Designing roads, water systems or buildings means balancing codes, budgets and site conditions, then coordinating many contractors. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 3.88 out of 5 for civil engineers, and systems analysis and time management at 3.75. Construction management, materials science and environmental planning use those skills. Most matches need no new degree. The gaps are running equipment and quality checks.
tips: Construction management is the most common switch and keeps you on projects you already know.
Architectural and Engineering Managers earn $171,270, which is 70% more, after years of project leadership.
Materials Scientists earn $117,790, or 17% more, if you enjoy lab and testing work.

faq.q: What jobs can former civil engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are architects (81%), Construction Managers (80%) and Water Resource Specialists (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Brownfield redevelopment specialists are also 77% matched, with a median of $141,900 for their broader BLS group, and use your site and environmental knowledge.

faq.q: Which careers for civil engineers pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more than $100,840. Architectural and engineering managers earn $171,270 (70% more), Database Architects $139,500 (38% more) and Materials Scientists $117,790 (17% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Engineering management usually needs a graduate degree or long experience.

faq.q: Do civil engineers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than civil engineers already have, and 3 usually need a graduate degree, including architecture. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 40% of workers in a close match, and your professional engineering license is valued in most of these roles.

faq.q: What skills should civil engineers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, quality control analysis, judgment and decision making and coordination. Operations analysis already rates 3.62 out of 5 for civil engineers in O*NET, so leading people on site is the main step toward management.
